The '''1982–83 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|81st season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|52nd consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
Club legend [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] came back to the club as head coach in a high-expected movement after he was [[La Liga]] champion managing [[Valencia CF]] in [[1970–71_Valencia_CF_season|1971]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://elpais.com/diario/1982/05/15/deportes/390261606_850215.html|work=El País|title=Di Stefano comes with no conditions|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=15 May 1982}}</ref> The arrive of Di Stefano as the team head coach was delayed by then club president [[Santiago Bernabéu (footballer)|Santiago Bernabeu]] -who died in 1978– after personal issues aroused since 1964 when the Argentine striker rejected his offer to retire with an administrative spot in the club and chose to play two more seasons with [[RCD Espanyol]]. 

Finally, after a long turmoil lasting almost a year Incumbent Luis de Carlos won the reelection as President of the club on 9 October 1982 defeating the electoral campaign of challenger [[Ramon Mendoza]] by more than 3,000 votes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1982/10/12/deportes/403225203_850215.html|date=11 October 1982|title=My Continuity does not mean Stagnation|accessdate=2 July 2020|work=El País|author=José Damián González|language=Spanish}}</ref> Mendoza was linked by Cambio 16 magazine with Soviet Spy agency KGB,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2020/04/04/5e8856e846163ffb528b45e1.html|title=A One of Ramon Mendoza and CIA-KGB|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=Spanish|date=4 April 2020|accessdate=1 July 2020}}</ref> prompting to quit his position as vice-president on board of directors during Autumn.

After a failed bid on [[Allan Simonsen]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 December 2023 |title=Forgotten EFL: When Charlton Athletic Signed a Ballon d’Or Winner – The Real EFL |url=https://therealefl.co.uk/2023/12/23/forgotten-efl-when-charlton-athletic-signed-a-ballon-dor-winner/ |access-date=26 December 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> De Carlos reinforced the club with low-profile players such as Dutch defender [[John Metgod]] from [[AZ Alkmaar]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1982/05/30/deportes/391557608_850215.html|date=29 May 1982|accessdate=2 July 2020|work=El País|title=Madrid transferred Metgod in and wants Lozano|language=Spanish}}</ref> English striker [[Laurie Cunningham]] suffered injury issues during almost the entire campaign and was loaned out by the club to [[Manchester United]] in April.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1983/07/27/deportes/428104803_850215.html|title=Cunningham asks Real Madrid another chance|work=El País|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=26 July 1983|language=Spanish}}</ref>

The campaign is best remembered by the bizarre fact of five trophies closely lost, four of them in four closely contested finals (Supercopa, European Cup Winners' Cup, Copa del Rey and Copa de La Liga). Besides that, in [[1982–83 La Liga|La Liga]] the squad finished in 2nd place a single point behind champions basque-side [[Athletic Bilbao]] after losing 0–1 against former Di Stefano club [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the ultimate match at Mestalla Stadium. Madrid were leading most of the rounds before the game and only needed a draw to clinch the title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://elpais.com/deportes/2019/03/31/actualidad/1554029857_223519.html|work=El País|title=The most exciting Valencia-Real Madrid match|language=Spanish|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=3 April 2019}}</ref>
